newsitem.title: USA: Dogs to check pedestrians at U.S. border bridges.
newsitem.headline: Dogs to check pedestrians at U.S. border bridges.

text.p: Drug-sniffing dogs will check pedestrians for illegal narcotics on the U.S.-Mexico bridges between El Paso and Ciudad Juarez, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.

About four million people walk across the four bridges each year. Police dogs are already used to search for drugs inside the 16 million cars that cross the bridges, but the decision to check pedestrians was forced by an increase in drug traffic.
Officials said an increase in vehicle searches over the last two years had pushed traffickers into concealing the drugs on their bodies and walking across the border.
The dogs will sniff at pedestrians from several feet away as they cross the bridges and alert their handlers by sitting when they detect the smell of narcotics.
Two dogs are to be assigned to the pedestrian watch immediately, but another 32 will be made available by the end of the year.
"We are encountering more and more pedestrians and passengers in vehicles who are carrying drugs," said Carol Rackley, the U.S. Customs Service port director in El Paso.
Rackley said she did not expect people to be frightened by the animals. "These dogs will act in a calm, unexcitable manner," she said.

U.S. Customs agents in El Paso made 1,136 drug seizures and confiscated 110,000 pounds (49,896 kg) of marijuana, cocaine and heroin in the 1996 fiscal year, up from 734 seizures and 73,000 pounds (33,112 kg) in 1995.
